newsitem.title: UK: Overseas investment in UK engineers up - survey.
newsitem.headline: Overseas investment in UK engineers up - survey.

text.p: Overseas takeovers in the UK engineering sector rose sharply this year, according to the latest survey by KPMG Corporate Finance.

Its ninth survey of global takeover activity showed the value of overseas takeovers of British engineering, electrical and electronic companies rose to almost $1.4 billion --up 25 percent on the same period last year.
Demand was particularly high for mechanical engineering firms, said KPMG which surveyed around 2,300 cross-border deals.

But UK engineers were more cautious in their foreign acquisitions, with the value of such deals at less than $600 million in the first six months of the year, compared with almost $2 billion last year.
Overseas deals involving manufacturing engineers fell to 325 million from $1.4 billion, but electrical and electronic firms raised foreign investment.
"The UK's technological edge and the quality of our engineers are the real magnets for inward investment," said Stephen Barrett, head of engineering at KPMG Corporate Finance.

"Foreign acquisition may not be a threat to the future of our manufacturing base, as some have argued, as long as the new proprietors continue UK production and continue investing in the businesses they have acquired."
He added that consolidation was happening at the smaller end of the scale, leaving scope for more bigger deals in future.
